B. Is this measure already running in Satakunta wellbeing services county (or in the Tyks university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit. Every current smoker with suspected lung cancer gets cessation medication and counselling at the first visit, as part of preparing for curative treatment.
effect_summary_en: In a Moscow cohort of 517 current smokers with early-stage (IA–IIIA) NSCLC, quitting after diagnosis was linked to lower all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53–0.85).
supported_en: Annals of Internal Medicine (2021): quitting after diagnosis was linked to an adjusted HR of 0.67 for all-cause mortality in early-stage NSCLC.
not_supported_en: The evidence does not show that quitting makes more patients eligible for curative treatment, and the result is observational, not from a Finnish trial.

in_use_summary_en: Satakunnan Kansa reported on 11 Nov 2026 that Sata's new lung cancer pathway, which started as a pilot in 2022 and became standard in 2024, includes support for quitting smoking.
missing_en: No page shows that every smoker gets cessation medication and counselling at the first specialist visit.
summary_en: According to Satakunnan Kansa (11 Nov 2026), Sata's lung cancer pathway, a 2022 pilot made standard in 2024, includes support for quitting smoking, but nothing says what that support is or whether every smoker gets medication at the first specialist visit. Tyks's lung cancer page does not mention quitting smoking. A 2021 Annals of Internal Medicine cohort study found that quitting after diagnosis was linked to an adjusted HR of 0.67 (0.53–0.85) for all-cause mortality in early-stage NSCLC, which matches the size we assume.
unanswered_en: No Sata or Tyks page was found that describes what the quit-smoking support in the pathway includes or when it is given.
